the area of the forest and its adjacency to other seminaturals are important factors in explaining recreational choices.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the landscape attributes of a forest recreational site are important in determining the choice of site, but that the effects of these landscape attributes depend on the choice-set definition.
the choice of recreational site is determined by the size and the adjacency of the forest patch.
the size of a patch and the proximity of seminatural areas are important factors for recreational choice, and that the effect of the size of the patch is not monotonic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the landscape characteristics that we identified are important for recreational choices, and that the choice set needs be larger than what is usually used in choice modelling.
recreational behaviour in forests is influenced by the characteristics of the surrounding landscape and the characteristics of the forest patch.
the size of a recreational area is an important attribute for the decision-making process of a visitor, but the size of the area is not the only important attribute.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of recreational site is strongly influenced by the surrounding landscape, and that GIS-based choice modelling offers an attractive tool for investigating these relationships.

GIS-based modelling of recreational behaviour is a promising tool for analysing the effects of landscape attributes on recreational choices and that GIS-based choice modelling can provide new insights for forest management and planning.
GIS and discrete choice modelling are powerful tools for modelling recreational choice and that the use of high-resolution data is important to obtain accurate estimates.
